q: Metal P displaces metal Q from a solution of Q ions. Metal Q displaces metal R from a solution of R ions. R does not displace P or Q. What is the order of reactivity, most reactive first?
explain: A metal displaces only the ions of less reactive metals, so P is more reactive than Q, and Q more reactive than R.

q: Which pair of metals react with cold water?
explain: Potassium and calcium react with cold water; zinc, iron and the metals below them do not react with it.

q: Why is potassium stored under oil?
options: It is a liquid that would evaporate
It is a gas at room temperature
It is toxic to the air
It reacts rapidly with oxygen and water vapour in air
explain: Potassium is so reactive that it quickly tarnishes and reacts with moisture, so the oil keeps air and water away.

q: Which equation correctly represents sodium reacting with water?
explain: Sodium and water give sodium hydroxide solution and hydrogen, and the equation balances with 2 Na, 4 H and 2 O on each side.

q: Which row correctly describes the reactions of calcium?
explain: Calcium is high in the series so it reacts with both cold water and dilute hydrochloric acid, whereas copper and silver react with neither.

q: Metal X displaces metal Y from a solution of Y ions. Which statement is correct?
options: Y forms positive ions more readily than X
X is lower in the reactivity series than Y
X has a smaller tendency to lose electrons than Y
X forms positive ions more readily than Y
explain: A displacing metal is higher in the series, so it loses electrons and forms positive ions more readily.

q: Which metal reacts most vigorously with cold water?
explain: Calcium is the highest in the series of the four, and zinc and iron do not react with cold water.

q: Which equation represents iron reacting with dilute hydrochloric acid?
explain: Iron forms iron(II) chloride with hydrogen, and the equation needs 2HCl to balance.

q: 1.30 g of zinc reacts with excess dilute hydrochloric acid: Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂. What volume of hydrogen forms at room temperature and pressure? (Ar: Zn = 65; 1 mol of gas = 24 000 cm³)
explain: Moles of Zn = 1.30 ÷ 65 = 0.020 mol, which gives 0.020 mol H₂, so the volume is 0.020 × 24 000 = 480 cm³.

q: A piece of zinc is added to dilute hydrochloric acid. Which observation is correct?
options: A steady stream of bubbles forms and the zinc gets smaller
explain: Zinc reacts at a moderate rate, giving hydrogen bubbles as the metal dissolves.

q: An iron nail is placed in blue copper(II) sulfate solution. Which observation is correct?
options: The nail dissolves and the solution becomes darker blue
The nail and the solution do not change
The nail gets a brown coating and the solution becomes pale green
The nail gets a silvery coating and the solution stays blue
explain: Iron displaces copper, which coats the nail, and Fe²⁺ ions give a pale green solution.

q: Silver does not react with dilute hydrochloric acid. What does this show?
options: Silver is less reactive than hydrogen
Silver is more reactive than hydrogen
Silver is more reactive than zinc
explain: A metal that cannot displace hydrogen from an acid is below hydrogen in the reactivity series.

q: Which conditions are needed for iron to rust?
explain: Rusting needs both water and oxygen to be present.

q: What is rust?
explain: Rust is hydrated iron(III) oxide, formed when iron reacts with oxygen and water.

q: Three iron nails are left for a week. Tube A has dry air (anhydrous calcium chloride), tube B has boiled water covered with a layer of oil, and tube C has air and water. In which tubes do the nails rust?
explain: Only tube C has both water and oxygen, since A has no water and B has no dissolved oxygen.

q: Which method of rust prevention does not work by excluding oxygen and water?
explain: A magnesium block is a sacrificial metal that corrodes in place of iron, whereas the other methods form a barrier.

q: How does painting an iron gate prevent rusting?
options: It makes the iron less reactive chemically
It stops oxygen and water from reaching the iron
It removes oxygen from the iron
It reacts with water to make an acid
explain: Paint forms a barrier, and with no contact with oxygen and water the iron cannot rust.

q: Which barrier method is most suitable for the moving chain of a bicycle?
explain: Grease stays on moving parts and excludes water and air, while paint or plastic would crack or wear away.

q: Why must a barrier coating on iron remain unbroken?
options: A gap lets hydrogen escape from the iron
A gap makes the coating react with the iron
A gap makes the iron more reactive
A gap lets oxygen and water reach the iron
explain: The barrier works only by keeping oxygen and water away, so any crack allows rusting to start.

q: Which statement about rusting is correct?
options: Aluminium and copper also rust to form iron(III) oxide
Rust forms from iron and nitrogen
All metals rust in the same way
explain: Rusting is the corrosion of iron and steel, as rust is hydrated iron(III) oxide, which needs iron.

q: A galvanised bucket is scratched through the zinc layer. Why does the exposed iron still not rust quickly?
options: Zinc is less reactive than iron, so the iron is protected
The scratch fills with rust that seals the surface
Zinc forms a barrier that cannot be broken
Zinc is more reactive than iron, so the zinc corrodes in preference
explain: Zinc loses electrons more readily than iron, so it is sacrificed and protects the iron even when the coating is broken.

q: Which statement explains sacrificial protection of iron by zinc?
options: Iron atoms lose electrons more readily and give them to zinc
Zinc atoms lose electrons in preference to iron atoms, so zinc corrodes instead
Zinc forms covalent bonds with iron
Zinc atoms gain electrons from iron atoms
explain: Zinc is higher in the reactivity series, so it loses electrons more easily and corrodes in place of iron.

q: Which metal could be attached to the iron pipe as a sacrificial block?
explain: A sacrificial metal must be more reactive than iron, and magnesium is above iron while the others are below it.

q: Iron is coated with a thin layer of copper, and then the coating is scratched to expose the iron. What is likely to happen?
options: The iron may rust because copper is less reactive and gives no sacrificial protection
The copper corrodes first and protects the iron
The scratch is sealed by the copper
The iron cannot rust as copper is a barrier
explain: Copper is below iron in the series, so once the barrier is broken the iron is not protected sacrificially.

q: Which row correctly describes a method of protecting iron?
explain: A zinc coating is a barrier and, because zinc is more reactive than iron, also gives sacrificial protection; paint, grease and plastic are only barriers.

q: Why does rusting continue until an iron object is destroyed?
options: Rust flakes off, exposing fresh iron to oxygen and water
Rust forms a layer that is more reactive than iron
Rust increases the amount of oxygen in the metal
Rust cannot form a flaky layer
explain: Rust is porous and flakes away, so new iron is exposed and the rusting carries on.

q: Which change would slow down the rusting of an iron nail?
options: Putting it in a sealed bottle with water and air
explain: Grease excludes oxygen and water, while the other conditions keep both present.

q: An iron nail does not rust in boiled water covered with a layer of oil. Why?
options: There is no water in the tube
There is no oxygen reaching the nail
The oil reacts with the iron
explain: Boiling removes dissolved oxygen and the oil layer stops air redissolving, so oxygen is missing.

q: An iron nail does not rust in a stoppered tube containing anhydrous calcium chloride. Which condition is missing?
explain: Anhydrous calcium chloride absorbs water vapour from the air in the tube, so water is missing.

q: A block of zinc is attached to the steel hull of a ship as sacrificial protection. What eventually happens to the block?
options: It corrodes away and needs replacing
It becomes a thicker coating of rust
explain: The zinc loses electrons in preference to the iron, so it is gradually used up and must be replaced.
